conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: B answers the operations lead's core question — what 35 members on Team actually costs — in the page headline ($420/month or $4,200/year) with zero interaction required, and the highlight tracks the billing toggle state. B also provides working controls for both sanctioned next actions (Start Team trial button and a real Contact sales button), while A renders 'Contact sales' as inert paragraph text with no affordance. At 390px, B restructures the comparison into stacked per-criterion groups that stay fully legible, whereas A's 14-row table has min-width 640px and requires horizontal scroll, appearing clipped in the capture. A is stricter on the closed fact set — its 'Not stated' discipline is exemplary and B invents two table cells (Enterprise 'Unlimited workspaces', 'Standard' support tier) — but those inventions sit in rows that do not distort the core Starter-vs-Team-vs-Enterprise decision for a 35-person team, while A's gaps directly slow the stated job. Both give a supported fit reason with no popularity claims. Evidence viewed: desktop, 390px states, interaction and state captures, sanitized source for both.
suspected_unblinding: none — both packets share the same sanitized static-starter README scaffolding and neither source tree nor captures contain treatment-identifying markers (the only 'baseline' hits are CSS align-items: baseline). A's README describes its own build discipline ('nothing is invented') but does not identify a treatment.

findings.label: A
findings.description: The answer to the visitor's central question — what 35 members costs — is not surfaced at the top level. The headline is generic ('Choose the right plan for your team') and the $420/month figure sits inside the Team card below the calculator; the annual figure appears only after operating the toggle. The information is present and correct, but the hierarchy makes the user assemble it rather than presenting it.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The Monthly/Annual control uses a two-sided switch with labels on both flanks, a pattern whose selected side can read ambiguously from the knob alone. Mitigated here: the aria-label updates to 'Billing: Monthly/Annual selected', the headline highlight moves with the state, and the table price cell switches cadence. Polish-level only.
